title.narrative: Affordable Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (A-RAS) to small-scale fish farmers in Nyeri, Kenya

description.narrative: This feasibility study tests and enhances the practicality of two new technological designs of affordable Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (A-RAS constructions) among small scale farmers in Kenya. Clean sufficient water is a scarce asset in Sub-Saharan Africa in general, including in Kenya. With Recirculation Aquaculture Systems (RAS), water use is expected to be reduced with 80-90%, while even with this reduced water use, fish production can go up (up to) 40x compared to the current practice. The effectiveness of the components that are locally available, locally designed and with manufacturing capabilities, smart and innovative combinations of affordable sensors and algorithm technology, and use of solar energy (SDG13) will be assessed.The reduction of fish farmer water use and the increase in fish production will be analysed. The long term ambition is to prepare for making the A-RAS constructions (System 1 and System 2) accessible to thousands of fish farmers, so that a large-scale use after project time can deal with a series of challenges including urgent problems of water recirculation (SDG6) and undernourishment of millions of people (SDG2) caused by limited clean water accessibility across African countries.
